newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian govt favours Tractebel, Electrabel merger.
newsitem.headline: Belgian govt favours Tractebel, Electrabel merger.

text.p: The Belgian government is in favour of a merger of Belgian utility holding company Tractebel SA with its unit Electrabel, a spokeswoman for Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Wednesday.

She added that Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) and French Compagnie de Suez had indicated that they had no objection to such a merger. Tractebel is owned by SGB, which is owned by Suez.
Electrabel, which has the largest capitalisation on the Brussels bourse, has a virtual monopoly on electricity production in Belgium.

Dehaene's spokeswoman, commenting on an article in Belgian financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd, told Reuters that Dehaene had spoken with Suez head Gerard Mestrallet and SGB head Etienne Davignon, where he had suggested the merger. She added the two business men had voiced no objection.
She said Dehaene confirmed the conversation in a letter to Davignon, which contained the following sentence:

"Finally, the governent considers that in the long run a merger between Tractebel and Electrabel is the best way to safeguard Tractebel's autonomy and Belgian interests, notably in matters of energy policy and employment."
"During our meeting of March 11, 1997 with Mr. Mestrallet and yourself, you have indicated that neither you or Mr. Mestrallet had any principal objection against this merger," the letter continued.
Spokesmen for SGB, Tractebel and Electrabel were not immediately available for comment.
A spokesman for the Brussels bourse said that trade in shares of Tractebel and Electrabel would not be suspended today as the merger idea was a long-term project.
The Financieel-Economische Tijd said that Suez chairman Gerard Mestrallet had approved the merger idea in writing.
A joining-up of the two would dispel fears over the impact of the planned merger between Suez and French utility group Lyonnaise des Eaux on Tractebel, the paper said.
The Belgian government has repeatedly expressed fears that following the Suez-Lyonnaise merger the foreign expansion of Tractebel would become subordinate to the French group's ambitions.

To counter such worries Tractebel plans a change in its articles of incorporation later this month, which will turn the group into a so-called "autonomous company". Several independent board members will be named to the board with that aim.
A Tractebel-Electrabel merger would be the final mega-operation in a long consolidation trend in the Belgian utility industry.
Earlier this month Tractebel shareholders approved the planned merger with Tractebel's foreign energy unit Powerfin .
That merger, which will be finalised in October, will reduce SGB's Tractebel stake to just over 50 percent from the current 65 percent. The merged group will have 42 percent of Electrabel.
The paper said a Tractebel-Electrabel merger would further dilute SGB's Tractebel stake to around 25 percent.
Tractebel has a bourse capitalisation of 213 billion francs, Electrabel one of 442 billion francs, together they would represent about one seventh of total Belgian stock market capitalisation.
